name: E2B
description: Manage E2B cloud sandboxes for AI agents: list, start, inspect, pause, resume and extend sandboxes, read their logs and CPU, memory and disk metrics, and browse the team's templates, builds and snapshots.
prerequisites: An E2B account (e2b.dev) and a team API key from the dashboard. Running sandboxes are billed per second to the team (the Hobby plan starts with free credits). About 2 minutes.

E2B_API_KEY.label: E2B API key
E2B_API_KEY.help: e2b.dev/dashboard, Keys (team API keys). The key acts for the whole team: it can start sandboxes billed to it.
E2B_API_KEY.patternMessage: Paste the API key as E2B shows it, starting with e2b_, without spaces. An access token (sk_e2b_...) does not work here.

verifyHints.401: E2B refused the API key. Copy a team API key (e2b_...) again from https://e2b.dev/dashboard?tab=keys; personal access tokens do not work here.
verifyHints.rate_limited: E2B rate limited the key or the team reached its limit of concurrent sandboxes. Wait, or kill sandboxes that are no longer needed.

instructions:
## E2B
This connector uses the **E2B control-plane API** (`https://api.e2b.app`): it manages the team's cloud sandboxes (small isolated Linux VMs that AI agents use to run code), reads their logs and resource metrics, and lists templates, builds and snapshots.

**Paid calls**: `e2b_create_sandbox` starts a sandbox and `e2b_resume_sandbox` restarts a paused one; a running sandbox is billed per second for its CPU and memory until it times out, is paused or is killed. `e2b_set_sandbox_timeout` extends that time. Confirm with the user before starting sandboxes or extending them, keep `timeout` short, and pause or let them expire when done. Reads cost nothing.

**Setup (2 minutes)**
1. Sign in at https://e2b.dev/dashboard.
2. Open **Keys** (https://e2b.dev/dashboard?tab=keys) and copy a team API key (it starts with `e2b_`).
3. Paste it into `E2B_API_KEY`. It is sent in the `X-API-Key` header.
4. Run `e2b_list_sandboxes` to check it.

**Workflow**
- Templates: `e2b_list_default_templates` shows E2B's ready-made templates (e.g. `base`, `code-interpreter-v1`, `desktop`) with CPU, memory and disk; `e2b_list_templates` the team's own templates with aliases, build status and spawn counts; `e2b_list_template_builds` the builds of one template.
- Start: `e2b_create_sandbox` with `template_id` (template id or alias, default `base`), a `timeout` in seconds (default 300), optional `metadata` (string key-value pairs to find it again), `env_vars`, `auto_pause` and `allow_internet_access`. The answer has the `sandboxID` and `domain`.
- Inspect: `e2b_list_sandboxes` (filter by `state` running or paused, `template`, `metadata` such as `user=abc&app=prod`, `started_after`); `e2b_get_sandbox` for one sandbox's template, resources, start and end time, state and network settings; `e2b_get_sandbox_logs` for its system and process logs; `e2b_get_sandbox_metrics` for CPU, memory and disk use over time.
- Lifecycle: `e2b_set_sandbox_timeout` sets a new end time counted from now (the plan caps it: 1 hour on Hobby, 24 hours on Pro); `e2b_pause_sandbox` freezes it with its memory and files (paused sandboxes are not billed for compute); `e2b_resume_sandbox` resumes a paused sandbox (or just extends a running one); `e2b_list_snapshots` lists saved snapshots.

**Switched off at install**: `e2b_kill_sandbox`; it cannot be undone (the sandbox and its files are gone), so an admin switches it on when the team needs it.

**Running code inside a sandbox is not part of this connector.** Commands, files and the code interpreter are served by the sandbox itself (its envd agent on `https://<port>-<sandboxID>.e2b.app`), not by this API: every sandbox has its own host and its own access token, process output is streamed, and the team API key must not be sent into a sandbox where generated code runs. Use the E2B SDKs (`e2b`, `@e2b/code-interpreter`) for that, or point the agent at a tool that wraps them.

**Reading answers**: times are ISO 8601, UTC; metric timestamps and log `cursor` values are Unix (metrics `start` and `end` in seconds, log cursors in milliseconds). `cpuCount` is vCPUs, `memoryMB` and `diskSizeMB` megabytes. The sandbox access tokens are removed from answers.

**Paging**: `e2b_list_sandboxes`, `e2b_list_templates`, `e2b_list_template_builds` and `e2b_list_snapshots` return the next page token in `_headers.x-next-token` (the list itself is under `data` when the answer is a list); pass it as `next_token` until it is missing. `e2b_list_sandboxes` also returns `_headers.x-total-running`.

**Errors**: 400 bad parameter (e.g. a timeout over the plan's maximum); 401 invalid key; 403 the team may not use the template; 404 unknown sandbox or template (a sandbox that timed out is gone); 409 the sandbox is already paused or being paused; 429 too many concurrent sandboxes or requests, wait and do not loop; 500 and 503 E2B-side errors.

tools.name: e2b_list_sandboxes
tools.description: List the E2B sandboxes of the team, newest first: sandbox id, template, alias, state (running or paused), start and end time, CPU, memory, disk and metadata. Free. Next page token in _headers.x-next-token.

state.description: Only sandboxes in this state; default both.

template.description: Only sandboxes of this template id or alias.

metadata.description: Metadata filter as key=value pairs joined by &, e.g. user=abc&app=prod.

started_after.description: Only sandboxes started at or after this ISO 8601 time.

order.description: Sort by start time, default desc (newest first).

tools.name: e2b_get_sandbox
tools.description: Read one E2B sandbox: template and alias, state, start and end time, CPU, memory and disk, envd version, domain, internet access, network rules, lifecycle settings and metadata. Free.

sandbox_id.description: Sandbox id from e2b_list_sandboxes or e2b_create_sandbox.

tools.name: e2b_create_sandbox
tools.description: Start a new E2B sandbox from a template. COSTS MONEY: the team is billed per second of CPU and memory while it runs, until the timeout (default 300 seconds), a pause or a kill. Confirm with the user before starting one and keep the timeout short.

template_id.description: Template id or alias, default base; e.g. code-interpreter-v1 or a team template from e2b_list_templates.

timeout.description: Lifetime in seconds, default 300. Hobby allows up to 3600, Pro up to 86400.

auto_pause.description: true pauses the sandbox at the timeout instead of killing it.

allow_internet_access.description: false blocks all outgoing internet traffic. Default true.

metadata.description: String key-value pairs to find the sandbox again, e.g. {"user": "abc"}.

env_vars.description: Environment variables for processes in the sandbox, as string key-value pairs. Do not pass secrets the user has not approved.

tools.name: e2b_set_sandbox_timeout
tools.description: Set when an E2B sandbox ends: timeout seconds counted from now, replacing the previous end time (a shorter value ends it sooner). Extending it keeps the sandbox billed for longer: confirm with the user.

timeout.description: Seconds from now until the sandbox ends.

tools.name: e2b_pause_sandbox
tools.description: Pause a running E2B sandbox, saving its files and, by default, its memory, so it can be resumed later with e2b_resume_sandbox. A paused sandbox is not billed for compute.

sandbox_id.description: Sandbox id of a running sandbox.

memory.description: false saves only the file system; resuming then reboots the sandbox. Default true.

tools.name: e2b_resume_sandbox
tools.description: Resume a paused E2B sandbox (or extend a running one) and return its details. COSTS MONEY: the resumed sandbox is billed per second again until the timeout. Confirm with the user before resuming.

timeout.description: Seconds from now until it ends again, default 300. A running sandbox's end time is only extended, never shortened.

memory.description: false resumes from the saved files only (cold boot). Default true.

tools.name: e2b_kill_sandbox
tools.description: Kill an E2B sandbox immediately. Its processes, memory and files are gone and cannot be restored. Installed switched off. Confirm the sandbox id with the user before calling.

tools.name: e2b_get_sandbox_logs
tools.description: Read the logs of one E2B sandbox (system and process output) with timestamp, level and message; filter by minimum level or a search string. Free.

search.description: Case-sensitive text the message must contain.

direction.description: forward (oldest first) or backward (newest first) from the cursor.

cursor.description: Start at this Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

tools.name: e2b_get_sandbox_metrics
tools.description: Read the resource use of one E2B sandbox over time: CPU count and usage percent, memory and disk used and total, per timestamp. Free.

start.description: Start of the interval, Unix seconds.

end.description: End of the interval, Unix seconds.

tools.name: e2b_list_templates
tools.description: List the team's E2B templates: template id, aliases and names, build id and status, CPU, memory and disk, public flag, spawn count, last spawn and dates. Free. Next page token in _headers.x-next-token.

tools.name: e2b_list_template_builds
tools.description: List the builds of one E2B template with build id, status, CPU, memory, disk, envd version and dates. Free. Next page token in _headers.x-next-token.

tools.name: e2b_list_default_templates
tools.description: List E2B's ready-made default templates (such as base, code-interpreter-v1 and desktop) with their aliases, CPU, memory, disk and envd version. Free.

tools.name: e2b_list_snapshots
tools.description: List the team's E2B sandbox snapshots with id, name, the sandbox they came from and dates; filter by sandbox or name. Free. Next page token in _headers.x-next-token.

name.description: Snapshot name or id, optionally tag-qualified (my-team/my-snapshot).
